target.title: test(qa): assert full Crabline selection metadata
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The QA CLI runtime tests only asserted the Crabline channel id in some smoke-ci and suite command paths. That left the rest of the resolved selection payload (`capabilityMatrixPath` and `smokeArtifactPath`) effectively unguarded, so a future refactor could silently drop or change those fields without a focused regression.

## Why This Change Was Made

This tightens the existing QA assertions to check the full Crabline `channelDriverSelection` object wherever the runtime is expected to resolve the default telegram channel. That keeps the manifest-driven capability and smoke artifact metadata covered alongside the channel id itself.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. This only strengthens regression coverage around QA Crabline selection metadata so smoke-ci and suite command wiring stay aligned with the current runtime contract.

## Evidence

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-qa.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw


 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  83 passed (83)
   Start at  22:35:25
   Duration  10.90s (transform 2.77s, setup 418ms, import 5.14s, tests 5.05s, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 20.78s
```

- Tightened the smoke-ci profile assertion to require the full Crabline selection payload
- Tightened the direct suite-command default-channel assertion to require the full Crabline selection payload
